publication.name: Small Bets, Costly Signals
publication.author: L. "Magpie" Pinette
publication.tagline: I worked as a Machine Learning Engineer, attempted a linguistics PhD, and taught English to Koreans and Turks. I'm now pursuing self-employment & writing about that here, as well as AI, cogsci, and life in a world we made but aren’t made for.

posts.title: Slime molds in a Chinese room – what LLM performance tells us about steelmanning the Turing test
posts.subtitle: I have been describing how LLMs operate as "slime molds in a Chinese room." This tends to raise some questions, and so in this post I am outlining my thinking behind the description.
posts.author: L. "Magpie" Pinette
posts.view_revised_quote: In undergrad I basically believed in this steelmanned Turing test : I believe that if an AI could pass this stronger version of the test it would require thinking like a human. I no longer believe that, and a substantial part of that is that I have a much better understanding than the average person of how LLM’s work right now, hence my “slime mold in a Chinese room” descriptor.
